speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
text: asked the Minister for Communications and Information what are the Ministry’s plans to ensure that all students have easy and low-cost access to high-speed Internet outside of school.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
text: IMDA's digital access programmes are complemented by MOE's provisions for students to access the Internet to support Home-Based Learning.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
text: Students also had the option to return to school to use computing facilities.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
text: Alternatively, students may also tap on Wireless@SG deployed at public spaces, like the public libraries and Community Clubs (CC), for free out-of-home Internet connectivity.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
text: Citizens’ needs evolve, and the Government reviews our initiatives to ensure citizens from needy households also have access to affordable high-speed Internet.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
text: This is able to support a typical family for common daily activities, such as video calls and video streaming.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Communications and Information (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
text: The Government will continue to review our provisions to meet the digital connectivity needs of students outside school.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: One question is, given the proliferation of more digital and online educational resources and the increase in home-based learning, I was wondering whether the Ministry will consider further expanding the provision for Home Access programmes beyond the two years to better serve those in disadvantaged circumstances and give them more accessibility, especially outside of school and having to be at home?
